subject: Backup delete propagation choreography & forensic traces — clarification
messages:
From: Legal Ops (Acme Bank) <legal.ops@acmebank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Backup delete propagation — need traceability for audit

Hi Jordan,

Quick question from our controls team: when a customer requests data deletion, we need to demonstrate that backups are also enqueued for deletion and provide an ordered set of traces showing the propagation across regions and storage tiers. Specifically: 1) what is the maximum window between primary delete and backup expunge in typical cases, 2) what artifacts/logs can you provide to prove deletion occurred (timestamps, shard ids, replica ids), and 3) is there any case where a deleted object remains recoverable beyond the stated retention window?

Can you send a short bulleted reply we can share with internal auditors? If you have a sample trace file that maps a delete event to expunge events, that would help.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Legal Ops — Acme Bank
legal.ops@acmebank.com

--
Requested urgency: Moderate (audit prep)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Legal Ops (Acme Bank) <legal.ops@acmebank.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Backup delete propagation — need traceability for audit

Hi Maya,

Thanks for the clear ask. Short version up-front: primary delete -> tombstone recorded in metadata DB immediately; async background expunge jobs run per-region and per-tier; in typical steady-state the expunge completes within 24–72 hours for SSD-backed replicas and 3–7 days for deep cold/offsite snapshots. Edge cases (in-flight DR replication, legal holds, or KMS key rotation) can extend this window — we enumerate these below.

What Im attaching is a sanitized sample trace that maps a delete request to our expunge events (delete_trace_logs.csv). Grace and Rachel are looped in for details on retention policy matrix and forensic artifacts.

Primary artifacts we can provide:
- delete_request_id, primary_timestamp (ISO), affected_shard_ids
- tombstone_timestamp (metadata db)
- expunge_job_id(s) with region and replica ids
- storage-layer expunge confirmation (storage object deletion event id)
- audit digest (sha256) tying the set together

Edge cases to call out:
- Legal hold / litigation hold: deletion is paused until release — this turns deletion into a controlled workflow, not an automatic expunge.
- Cross-region replication lag: if a replica is mid-transfer it may require a background reconcile and re-enqueue; this can add hours.
- KMS key rotation / key destruction: if a key is destroyed, object becomes unreadable; we still track expunge events but the forensic artifact differs (encryption tombstone).

Next steps: Grace, can you confirm the retention tiers and expected SLA numbers for each? Priyom, can you add whether we can produce a single-line CSV per customer mapping of delete->expunge events on demand (for auditor export)?

Jordan Blake
Director, Cloud Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Legal Ops (Acme Bank) <legal.ops@acmebank.com>
Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2028 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Backup delete propagation — need traceability for audit

Hi all,

Quick matrix to clarify runbooks (high level):

Retention tier | Typical expunge window | Forensic artifact
- Hot (SSD replicas) | 24	72 hours | storage delete event + expunge_job_id
- Warm (object store regional) | 48	96 hours | storage delete event + replica manifest
- Cold/offsite snapshot | 3	7 days (depends on offsite window) | snapshot manifest + snapshot-expunge job id

We can produce the following per-request artifacts for auditors: delete_request_id, tombstone timestamp, expunge_job_ids (per region), storage event ids, and the manifest that lists object keys and sizes. We package these into a zipped forensic bundle.

Notes:
- If a customer has an active legal hold we do not run expunge until legal hold is removed; we provide the hold record instead.
- For customers using server-side encryption with a customer-managed key, expunge events are recorded but the key lifecycle has to be coordinated to prove non-recoverability (key destruction is a separate control).

Ive uploaded the retention matrix to the shared drive link below and attached a compact spreadsheet that maps tiers to job ids.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachment: backup-retention-matrix.xlsx
Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-company-retention-doc

Subject: Re: Backup delete propagation — need traceability for audit

Maya / Acme team,

Following up with some pragmatic notes from SRE/ops perspective so auditors get what they need without overwhelming them:

1) We can produce a single CSV (example attached) that lists: delete_request_id, primary_delete_ts, tombstone_ts, expunge_job_id(s), expunge_completion_ts, region, replica_id, storage_object_id.
2) We can redact customer payloads and provide checksums instead of raw objects.
3) For deeper forensics (block-level) we can coordinate with your audit window; that requires a 48-hour lead.

If you want, we can run a short demo export on a test tenant and show the chain live.

- Rachel
Senior SRE, Data Resiliency
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the detail. Two clarifying asks before we accept the artifacts into our scope: 1) can the CSV include the expunge_job log link (or job stdout snippet) for at least one example per tier, and 2) please confirm whether snapshots that are retained due to an ongoing DR run show an explicit re-enqueue event once the run completes.

If you can add those two items we should be able to close the evidence loop.

Regards,
Samir Patel
Lead Auditor, KPMG Cloud Compliance

Request: add sample job stdout and confirm re-enqueue semantics

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Backup delete propagation — need traceability for audit

Samir / team,

We can do both. Action items completed and attached:
- Added an example job stdout snippet to the forensic bundle (included as job_stdout_example.txt inside the zip).
- Confirmed: during a DR run we mark affected snapshots with a temporary "requeue_on_completion" flag; once the DR window closes the reconcile worker enqueues a follow-up expunge job and we record a reenqueue_event with timestamp and parent_job_id. That event is included in the CSV as reenqueue_event_ts and parent_job_id.

I'll hand off the final zipped forensic bundle to Jordan for delivery to Acme. Please advise if you want the demo export.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
